newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Bengang falls below offer price.
newsitem.headline: China's Bengang falls below offer price.

text.p: China's Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd B shares plunged to HK$2.00 in late morning trading on its debut on Tuesday compared with an offer price of HK$2.38 as investors shunned the steel sector play, brokers said.
"No one wants to buy the steel sector, especially when the rest of the market is caving in," an analyst at a major foreign bank told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
China has 2,000 steel factories, only 75 of which made a profit last year, analysts have said.
The company posted net profits of 361.5 million yuan for 1996 and 167.9 million yuan for 1995 under international accounting standards.
"When a new share debuts this way, you know the market is in trouble," the analyst said.
The hard currency B index plunged 5.25 percent to trade at 120.98 points in late morning.
Shenzhen's A and B share markets have been hit by a long string of rumoured and actual government measures to cool the over-heated stock markets.

The company in June completed an initial public offering of 400 million B shares, carrying a price-earnings (P/E) ratio of eight times based on a fully diluted 1996 per-share net profit of 0.318 yuan under international accounting standards.
